Changing South Caucasus: Time for EU Leadership

发布源: European Centre for International Political Economy (ECIPE) --Belgium | 抓取时间: 2026-10-30

By Ambassador Teimuraz Janjalia, Senior Fellow, EU Awareness Centre

The South Caucasus is a strategic crossroad of Europe, Asia, and the Middle East, and its geopolitical significance has grown markedly in the past six years. The development is driven by regional and systemic shocks such as the 2020 Karabakh war, Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine, and the rapid reconfiguration of transit and energy corridors, most notably the Trans-Caspian Middle Corridor. At the same time, regional powers such as Turkey, China, and Iran have become more assertive, and the United States is clearly renewing its strategy for the region. These transformations elevate the region’s importance for Europe and its ambitions for connectivity, supply-chain resilience, and energy diversification. They introduce complex challenges but also present opportunities for the European Union’s traditional framework of engagement.

Currently, the European Union has a broad and diverse range of instruments and institutional frameworks for regional interaction. These mechanisms encompass bilateral relationships with Armenia, Azerbaijan, and Georgia, the long-standing multilateral architecture of the Eastern Partnership, the high-leverage Global Gateway Strategy with its connectivity platform, and the recently prioritised Black Sea Strategy. Transposing the Platform Work Directive: Comparative Assessment and Good Practic...

发布源: European Centre for International Political Economy (ECIPE) --Belgium | 抓取时间: 2026-10-30

Digital labour platforms are an increasingly important way of organising work across the European Union (EU), connecting consumers and businesses with people who provide services ranging from delivery and transport to software development and professional advice. The Platform Work Directive must be transposed by member states no later than 2 December 2026. Its implementation will determine whether people performing platform work can rely on effective protection and whether platforms face rules that are clear enough to support investment, compliance and cross-border activity.

The Directive addresses three practical issues. First, it requires EU countries to determine employment status according to how work is organised in practice, rather than the contractual label used. Second, it establishes safeguards for the use of personal data and automated systems, including transparency, human oversight and review of important decisions. Third, it requires platforms to provide public authorities and representatives of people performing platform work with specified information.

This study examines draft transposition measures in Austria, Czechia, Estonia, the Netherlands and Sweden. It assesses whether the national rules are clear, workable and proportionate for people performing platform work, platforms, intermediaries and public authorities. No draft provides a complete model. CitiesTake the Lead on Climate ActionThere is no secure and competitive Europe without sustainability. As European cities take the centre stage of this transition, the real challenge lies in delivering it under real economic and political constraints. To explore the path ahead, the Lisbon Council convened the2026 Sustainable Cities Summit on ‘Squaring the Green Circle: Climate Action, Economic Urgency, Urban Reality.’The summit served to launch theSustainable Cities Lab,a new initiative to move fromwhatmust be done tohowEurope delivers.

发布源: Lisbon Council for Economic Competitiveness and Social Renewal --Belgium | 抓取时间: 2026-10-30

There is no secure and competitive Europe without sustainability. And European cities now sit at the centre of the green transition: they are the primary markets for clean industry and the places where high-level European Union targets must be reconciled with the daily realities of housing, energy and mobility. While around 70% of European Union legislation is implemented at the local level, a persistent gap remains between climate ambition and actual delivery. To explore how to bridge this gap and turn policy into practice, the Lisbon Council convened the2026 Sustainable Cities Summit on ‘Squaring the Green Circle: Climate Action, Economic Urgency, Urban Reality,’bringing together leading policymakers, city practitioners, investors and urban innovators.

The summit opened with aHigh-Level Roundtable on ‘Scaling Sustainability in a Tougher Climate: What Europe’s Cities Have Learned and What Comes Next,’a candid, peer-to-peer exchange between senior city leaders and experts. From the lived experience of key cities, includingBrussels, Cluj-Napoca, Copenhagen, Firenze, Ferrara, Hamburg, Leuven, Madrid and Riga,the discussion highlighted what can realistically be replicated and scaled across diverse urban contexts.

item.content:encoded:
The Progressive Post

发布源: Foundation for European Progressive Studies (FEPS) --Belgium | 抓取时间: 2026-10-30

In this nightmare vision of cats in revolt, fifteen-year-old Alex and his friends set out on a diabolical orgy of robbery, rape, torture and murder. Alex is jailed for his teenage delinquency and the State tries to reform him - but at what cost?

With regional powers like Israel, Turkey, the Gulf States and Egypt, becoming increasingly assertive in the Mediterranean, this issue'sSpecial CoverageThe crowded sea: fragmentation around the Mediterranean, focuses on the role the EU could and should play in this changing landscape.

No matter how fast we run, much like in Lewis Carroll'sThrough the Looking-Glass, we struggle to catch up with AI's innovations. In ourFocusThe red queen's race: running faster to match the pace of AI, we consider how to make AI socially, economically and democratically sustainable.

Our firstDossier,Beyond implementation day: the Pact on Migration and Asylumexamines the uncertainties surrounding the pact's execution  as well as the human rights concerns raised by the approval of the Return Regulation by the European Parliament. And the secondDossierThe EU's industrial paradigm shiftfocuses on the European Commission's newly proposed Industrial Accelerator Act. Even though a noticeably more interventionist industrial strategy is proposed, the exact nature of the industrial Europe that is being shaped remains questionable.
